key_insight: In this small open-label trial, two supervised doses of psilocybin were associated with meaningful reductions in OCD symptoms.
clinical_relevance: The findings suggest psilocybin could be a promising adjunctive option for treatment-resistant OCD, but it is not yet established as standard care.
method: Waitlist-controlled open-label randomized clinical trial at Johns Hopkins.
37 adults with OCD and prior failed psychotherapy or pharmacotherapy attempts; 30 completed 1-month follow-up.
Two doses over 2 weeks: 20 mg psilocybin, then 30 mg if tolerated, with supportive monitoring.
evidence_signal: Compared with the waitlist group, the immediate-treatment group showed a significant drop in Y-BOCS scores, and improvement persisted after crossover treatment.
watch_item: Because the study was open-label and small, expectancy effects and limited generalizability remain important concerns.
paper_title: An Open-Label Multidose Psilocybin Intervention for Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder.
